sections.intro: Java 1.21.11 combat timing forms the foundation of every exchange in Unstable SMP FFA. Wind charges function as mobility first, cooldown second; they reposition you out of danger but also reset your attack timing, creating strategic moments where you trade offensive pressure for repositioning. Projectile arc timing matters for ranged consistency. Elytra and rocket timing unlock vertical play but introduce their own cooldowns. Launching upward costs seconds of vulnerability if enemies have ranged tools; you gain height but lose ground control until you land or glide to a new position. This vertical dimension forces you to choose between staying grounded for quick melee responses or gaining sightline advantage at the cost of mobility commitment. Combining elytra repositioning with a projectile like a trident or wind charge creates powerful sequences if timed correctly — reposition, then fire while your opponent is still recovering from your last ground exchange.

Wind charges, pearls, tridents, and TNT carts add utility for closing gaps, escaping pressure, or area denial. Master Java 1.21.11 cooldown timing for each weapon to maximize damage output.

faq.question: How do you survive Free For All with 100 soldiers in Unstable SMP FFA?
faq.answer: Free For All is player-versus-player combat in rotating arenas, not a 100-soldier wave mode. Simulator mode is where you face armies of up to 100 AI soldiers from NULL, The Law, Cindercrest, and the Kingdom of Unstable. You can play Simulator solo or form a party of up to 10 players, and the soldiers fight back and heal. Use cover, coordinate with party members, and prioritize high-threat targets to survive extended engagements.
